evals.name: feature-from-stale-develop
evals.prompt:
Get PAY-318 set up for me, I'll write the code myself. It's the monthly CSV export for the accountants. Criteria from the ticket:
- `python -m invoices export 2026-08` writes invoices-2026-08.csv
- one row per invoice issued that month, using the month query we already have
- header row: number, customer, issued_on, amount
- amount in rupees with two decimals (4800.50, not 480050)
evals.expected_output: A new branch feature/PAY-318-<PascalName> (CONTRIBUTING.md's convention) that starts at origin/develop, not at the checked-out local develop, which is three commits behind: it lacks invoices_for_month (the month query the second criterion relies on) and ADR 0007. The branch does not track origin/develop (push.default=upstream here). The fetch fails (origin unreachable) and the run says the base is only as fresh as the last fetch. Commit messages show an earlier start on PAY-318 on origin/feature/accountant-csv-export (branch name without the id; Dev Two, one stub commit cut from main without the month query), raised as a question, not ignored and not deleted. The tests at the new base are green only because the December test is an expected failure: 5 passed, 1 xfailed (test_december_includes_new_years_eve, PAY-305), meaning invoices_for_month returns nothing for December, which the export would inherit. The four criteria are restated, none added. The decision chain is read at the base: ADR 0004 (still marked Accepted) is superseded for accountant CSV files by ADR 0007 (only on origin/develop), so rupees with two decimals are allowed, but 0007 requires money columns named with the _inr suffix, so the header 'amount' is the open question for the ticket owner. Recommending amount_inr is fine if labelled as a recommendation. No code, no commit, no push, and no local git configuration changed for any existing branch (no upstream set on develop).
expectations: Exactly one new local branch exists, named feature/PAY-318-<Name> (Name two to four PascalCase words, id in capitals); it points at origin/develop's commit ('test(invoices): month query boundaries [PAY-301]'), not at the local develop, main or the earlier PAY-318 branch; `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref <branch>@{upstream}` reports no upstream or origin/<its own name>, never origin/develop; and it is checked out in the repository's checkout or in a worktree whose path the final message gives

The final message says the checked-out local develop is behind origin/develop (it lacks invoices_for_month, the 'month query we already have', and ADR 0007), that the branch was cut from origin/develop (or develop after fast-forwarding it) for that reason, and that the fetch from origin failed or was not made, so origin/develop is only as recent as this clone's last fetch

The final message reports the earlier work on this ticket found through its commit message, origin/feature/accountant-csv-export (commit 'wip: csv export stub [PAY-318]' by Dev Two, cut from main, without the month query), and raises it as a question (continue it, retire it, or coordinate with its author); the run does not delete, rename or reset that ref, and gives no command that deletes it unless conditioned on its author's agreement. A message that says no branch exists for PAY-318 fails

The run runs the tests (make check or pytest) on the new branch's code and the final message reports what the run printed: 5 passed and 1 xfailed (an expected failure, test_december_includes_new_years_eve, marked with PAY-305), not merely 'all green' or '5 passed'

The final message connects that expected failure to the ticket: invoices_for_month returns no invoices for December (its end date stays in the same year), so an export built on it would write no rows for any December month; it names PAY-305 or the xfail as a known, unfixed defect the ticket depends on, raised as a question or risk, and the run does not fix it

All four criteria from the request are recorded, in the final message or in a file in the repository, with their substance intact (the command writing invoices-2026-08.csv, one row per invoice of the month using the existing month query, the header number, customer, issued_on, amount, and amounts in rupees with two decimals), and no criterion the request did not give (empty months, sort order, quoting, an output flag, a coverage target) is presented as part of the ticket; such points appear only as the run's own labelled suggestions or questions

The final message applies the decision that holds at origin/develop for files produced for the accountants, ADR 0007: rupees with two decimals is allowed for this export and is not reported as a violation of the paise rule or as needing a new ADR; and it raises that 0007 requires money columns in such files to be named with the _inr suffix, so the ticket's header column 'amount' conflicts with it, as a question for the ticket owner. Recommending amount_inr is acceptable when labelled as the run's recommendation; presenting either header as settled, or recording either one in a file as the decision, fails. A message that reports the rupee criterion as contradicting the integer-paise rule (ADR 0004) without accounting for ADR 0007 fails

The run writes no implementation and changes nothing it was not asked to: no working tree differs from its HEAD in invoices/ or tests/ (no export command, no CSV code, no new or changed test, December bug not fixed); no commit is made (the new branch's tip is origin/develop's commit); main, v1.2.0 and every refs/remotes/origin/* ref are unchanged; the local develop is unchanged or fast-forwarded to origin/develop; nothing is pushed and no remote is changed; no tracked file is modified (a .gitignore line that only ignores the run's own notes is allowed); new files, if any, are notes about the task, contain no em dash, and mark any decision as Proposed without naming anyone as having decided it

The run leaves the clone's local git configuration as it found it, apart from what the new branch and a worktree the run made need: `git config --local --list` shows no upstream or other setting added or changed for develop, main or any other existing branch, push.default and the origin remote unchanged; and .git/info/exclude gains at most a line that ignores the run's own notes or worktree, which the final message mentions

evals.name: hotfix-with-work-in-progress
evals.prompt: Customers on prod are seeing GST rounded down, e.g. ₹100.25 at 18% comes out as ₹18.04 instead of ₹18.05. Cut me a hotfix branch for RATE-77 so I can get on it.
evals.expected_output: A hotfix/RATE-77-<PascalName> branch (RELEASING.md's convention) at tag v1.8.2, the version production runs: RELEASING.md says main is production and the newest tag is v1.8.3, but v1.8.3 (the RATE-65 slab preview) was rolled back by RATE-66 and deploy/production.yaml on main pins v1.8.2 again. A hotfix from main or v1.8.3 would re-ship the withdrawn slab preview, so the release path is a question, and the hotfix cannot be released as v1.8.3 (the tag exists); v1.8.4 is the next free number and will not contain 1.8.3's change. develop already has the fix, 'fix(gst): round GST half up to the paisa [RATE-61]', never released: the hotfix is a cherry-pick of it onto v1.8.2 (it touches only internal/gst and applies cleanly, which the run checks without committing), and develop needs no second fix. The engineer's checkout (feature/RATE-70-SlabRates) already contains RATE-61, so the bug is not visible there; its uncommitted work stays exactly where it is, not stashed, committed or carried over (a worktree or a branch created without switching). Baseline at v1.8.2: TestTax and TestSplitOddPaisaGoesToCGST pass, none covers half-up rounding. The hotfix carries nothing but the fix (no notes or progress file to commit with it). No fix is written in the repository, nothing committed, tagged or pushed.
expectations: Exactly one new branch exists, named hotfix/RATE-77-<Name> (Name two to four PascalCase words), pointing at the commit tagged v1.8.2 ('fix(api): reject rates above 100% [RATE-58]'); it contains neither 'feat(rates): slab preview endpoint [RATE-65]' nor 'chore(release): 1.8.3 [RATE-65]', so it was not cut from v1.8.3, main, develop or feature/RATE-70-SlabRates

The final message tells the user the branch starts at v1.8.2 because that is what production runs, gives the evidence the run found for it (deploy/production.yaml on main pinning v1.8.2, or the RATE-66 rollback commit), and says why neither main nor the newest tag v1.8.3 was used: both carry the RATE-65 slab preview that was withdrawn from production. A message that only names the base without the evidence, or that says main or v1.8.3 is what production runs, fails

The final message says the hotfix cannot simply be merged into main and released as RELEASING.md describes without also re-releasing RATE-65, and leaves how to release it (for example tagging from the hotfix branch, or reverting RATE-65 on main first) as a question or a labelled recommendation, not as something decided

The final message says the hotfix cannot be released as v1.8.3 because that tag already exists, names the next free version (v1.8.4) or leaves the number as an explicit question, and notes that a release built from v1.8.2 will not contain what v1.8.3 contained

The final message reports that develop already contains the fix, commit 'fix(gst): round GST half up to the paisa [RATE-61]' (unreleased), and proposes bringing that commit onto the hotfix branch (cherry-pick) rather than writing the rounding change again; it says the commit touches only internal/gst and applies cleanly onto v1.8.2, and the transcript shows a check the run made for that without leaving a commit (for example git apply --check, git merge-tree, or a cherry-pick in a throwaway export or worktree that is then discarded); a claim of clean application with no check behind it fails. It does not tell the user the fix still has to be written for develop or merged into develop as a new change

The engineer's uncommitted work is intact at the end: in a working tree that has feature/RATE-70-SlabRates checked out, internal/rates/slab.go still contains the uncommitted BlendedTax function, internal/rates/slab_test.go still contains TestBlendedTaxFirstSlabOnly, and the untracked internal/rates/council_table.go still exists, all with their fixture contents

The work in progress was never stashed or committed: `git stash list` is empty, and no commit object reachable from any ref, reflog entry of refs/stash, or worktree HEAD contains BlendedTax or internal/rates/council_table.go; feature/RATE-70-SlabRates still points at 'feat(rates): find the slab for an amount [RATE-70]'

The final message tells the user their uncommitted RATE-70 work was left untouched on feature/RATE-70-SlabRates, and gives where the hotfix branch can be worked on without that work: a worktree path that `git worktree list` shows with the hotfix branch checked out and none of internal/rates present, or, if it is checked out nowhere, a command that opens it in a separate worktree and would succeed as given. A worktree the run created and a printed command that would succeed pass equally. Offering to create a branch later does not pass

The final message's statement of what RATE-77 must achieve matches the request and the README's rule that GST is rounded half up to the nearest paisa (10025 paise at 1800 bps gives 1805 paise, not 1804); no other requirement is presented as part of the ticket, and further checks are labelled as the run's suggestions

The run runs the tests (make check or go test) on the v1.8.2 code, in the hotfix worktree or an export of that commit, and not only in the RATE-70 checkout (whose tests already include RATE-61's), judged from the transcript

The final message gives the baseline at v1.8.2 as the run observed it (the internal/gst tests pass, named or counted) and says that no test at v1.8.2 covers half-up rounding, so RATE-77 needs one (for example Tax(10025, 1800) giving 1805); reporting only 'tests pass' fails

The run writes no fix and changes nothing it was not asked to: internal/gst/gst.go and gst_test.go on the hotfix branch and in every working tree equal their content at that tree's HEAD (the cherry-pick is proposed, not performed); no test is added to the repository; no commit or tag is made (main, develop, feature/RATE-70-SlabRates, v1.8.1, v1.8.2, v1.8.3 unchanged, and every refs/remotes/origin/* ref unchanged unless moved by a fetch the final message reports; the only new ref is the hotfix branch); nothing is pushed and no remote changed; no tracked file is modified beyond the fixture's own uncommitted RATE-70 changes; new files, if any, are task notes or a worktree, absent from `git status` in the engineer's RATE-70 checkout, and contain no em dash

Nothing but the fix is set up to ship on the hotfix branch: no task notes, progress file or other file unrelated to the rounding fix is added to, staged in or committed on the hotfix branch, and the final message does not tell the user to commit notes or a progress file along with the fix; notes the run keeps, if any, live outside the hotfix tree or are ignored

evals.name: task-set-two-repos
evals.prompt: Start SHOP-12 OrderNotes across ShopApi and ShopWeb.
evals.expected_output: This session's repository is ShopApi (docs/architecture/repo-plan.json gives it path "."); ShopWeb is the sibling at ../ShopWeb. The run creates one branch, feature/SHOP-12-OrderNotes, in ShopApi only, from origin/develop, with no upstream; the fetch fails (origin unreachable) and it says so. It asks one question for the merge order with ShopApi first recommended (the server before the client, by the plan's git_path groups) and, with nobody to answer, takes that order. docs/progress/SHOP-12.md in ShopApi has a `## Repos` section `1. ShopApi (.)`, `2. ShopWeb (../ShopWeb)`, left uncommitted. The report prints the line to run in the sibling, `start-task SHOP-12 OrderNotes --type feature --repos ShopApi,ShopWeb`. Nothing is written, branched or committed in ShopWeb, and nothing is pushed.
expectations: Exactly one new branch exists in this repository (ShopApi): feature/SHOP-12-OrderNotes, pointing at origin/develop's commit ('docs: owners [SHOP-2]'), with no upstream or origin/feature/SHOP-12-OrderNotes as its upstream, never origin/develop

Nothing was written in the sibling ../ShopWeb: `git -C ../ShopWeb branch --list` shows only develop and main, `git -C ../ShopWeb status --porcelain --ignored` is empty, and ../ShopWeb has no .bearing directory and no docs/progress file

The run asked (or, with nobody to answer, recorded that it would ask) exactly one question about the merge order, with ShopApi first as the recommended option, and went on with ShopApi first; a run that asked about the order more than once, or recommended ShopWeb first, fails
docs/progress/SHOP-12.md exists in ShopApi with a `## Repos` section whose items are, in this order, `1. ShopApi (.)` and `2. ShopWeb (../ShopWeb)`, and the file is not committed

The final message prints the line to run in the sibling, `start-task SHOP-12 OrderNotes --type feature --repos ShopApi,ShopWeb` (the brief's `start-task SHOP-12 OrderNotes --repos ShopApi,ShopWeb` with the type the skill now adds), with the list in the settled merge order
The final message says the fetch from origin failed (or was not possible), so origin/develop is only as fresh as the last fetch

Nothing was committed or pushed: develop and main in ShopApi are unchanged, the new branch has no commit of its own, no `git push` was run, and `git diff fixture -- shopapi tests Makefile README.md docs/architecture` is empty
No file written or edited contains an em dash character

evals.name: bugfix-task-set-sibling-type
evals.prompt: Orders with a discount show the pre-discount total on the order page because the API sends the wrong total. Start SHOP-15 DiscountTotals as a bugfix across ShopWeb and ShopApi.
evals.expected_output: A bugfix task set: one branch bugfix/SHOP-15-DiscountTotals in this repository (ShopApi) from origin/develop, with no upstream. The repo plan puts the server (ShopApi, Shop/Server) before the client (ShopWeb, Shop/Client) although the request names ShopWeb first, so the one merge order question recommends ShopApi first and the run takes it. docs/progress/SHOP-15.md has `## Repos` with `1. ShopApi (.)` and `2. ShopWeb (../ShopWeb)`. The sibling line carries the type, `start-task SHOP-15 DiscountTotals --type bugfix --repos ShopApi,ShopWeb`, so ShopWeb starts the same bugfix/ branch rather than a feature/ one. Nothing is written in ShopWeb, nothing committed or pushed.
expectations: Exactly one new branch exists in ShopApi: bugfix/SHOP-15-DiscountTotals (a bugfix/ branch, not feature/), pointing at origin/develop's commit ('docs: owners [SHOP-2]'), never tracking origin/develop

The final message prints the sibling line with the set's type: `start-task SHOP-15 DiscountTotals --type bugfix --repos ShopApi,ShopWeb`; a sibling line without `--type bugfix` (which would start ShopWeb on feature/SHOP-15-DiscountTotals) fails

The merge order puts ShopApi first, from the repo plan's git_path groups (Server before Client), although the request named ShopWeb first; the one merge order question (asked or recorded) recommends ShopApi first, and the final message says why (the API provides what the web page consumes, or the plan's groups)
docs/progress/SHOP-15.md exists in ShopApi, uncommitted, with a `## Repos` section `1. ShopApi (.)` then `2. ShopWeb (../ShopWeb)`
Nothing was written in the sibling ../ShopWeb: its branches are still develop and main, `git -C ../ShopWeb status --porcelain --ignored` is empty and it has no .bearing directory

No fix was written and nothing was committed or pushed: `git diff fixture -- shopapi tests Makefile README.md docs/architecture` is empty, the new branch has no commit of its own, and no `git push` was run
No file written or edited contains an em dash character

evals.name: site-flow-recorded-in-task-branch
evals.prompt:
/start-task WEB-7 PricingPage --flow site

A pricing page for the marketing site: three plans side by side and a contact form for larger orders.
evals.expected_output: One branch feature/WEB-7-PricingPage from origin/main (the README's trunk rule; there is no develop), with no upstream; the fetch fails and the run says so. `--flow site` is given, so nothing is asked about the flow: the run records it with brg-config in the new branch's tree, leaving .bearing/config.json holding "flow": "site" uncommitted on feature/WEB-7-PricingPage, to be committed with the first change; main does not gain it. The baseline make check is reported as printed (check: 2 pages, check: passed). The next step is the site flow's page brief (Superpowers brainstorming), not a PRD or a design document. No page is written, nothing is committed or pushed.
expectations: Exactly one new branch exists: feature/WEB-7-PricingPage, pointing at origin/main's commit ('feat(about): about page [WEB-3]'), with no upstream or origin/feature/WEB-7-PricingPage as its upstream, never origin/main

With feature/WEB-7-PricingPage checked out (in this checkout, or a worktree whose path the final message gives), .bearing/config.json parses as JSON and its "flow" is "site"; the transcript shows it written with `brg-config set flow site` (or the file has exactly that content)

The flow is recorded in the task branch only and is not committed: .bearing/config.json is untracked (or uncommitted) on feature/WEB-7-PricingPage, `git log --all -- .bearing/config.json` lists no commit, and main is still 'feat(about): about page [WEB-3]'
No question was asked (or recorded) about whether this is a site: `--flow site` was given
The run ran make check on the new branch and reports what it printed (2 pages, check: passed), not a result it did not see

The final message names the site flow's next step: the page brief with Superpowers brainstorming (goal, audience, primary action, sections); it does not send the engineer to prd, high-level-design or openapi-spec

No page or component was written and nothing was committed or pushed: `git diff fixture -- src scripts Makefile package.json README.md` is empty, the new branch has no commit of its own, and no `git push` was run
No file written or edited contains an em dash character
